about_me.1: My name is Eryk Rozdolski, and I do what needs to be done. That is, if I believe something should be done and there isn't a more suitable person than me, I feel obligated to carry it out.
about_me.2: Since 2017, I have been working at Panie Kolego Projekt. I mainly focus on software development as a front-end developer. Thanks to my experience and interest in design, I find it easier to navigate topics related to UI/UX and design in general.
about_me.3: I've been fortunate to write commercially in many different languages, such as Python, OCaml, and JavaScript, which has allowed me to develop a broad paradigmatic perspective when it comes to my intuition about what clean code should look like. These days, I mainly write in JavaScript and work on problems related to web development in the broad sense.
about_me.4: I like to spend my free time actively; I played amateur football for a long time. I also dedicate quite a bit of time to other sports—lately more to jump rope and chess. From time to time I try to record my own music, and if that doesn't work out, I listen to others.

contact_text: If you have an interesting project for me or are looking for someone to collaborate with, let me know—I'll get back to you as soon as possible.
Software Development: In 2026, with the rapid development of AI tools, my approach to software design continues to rely on principles of writing clean—meaning stable—software that have been proven over the years. Code is read (maintained) more often than it is written. It's easier to maintain a smaller amount of code. The number of lines of code should be kept as low as possible, up to the point where readability is compromised. Conciseness, stability, and clarity are easiest for me to achieve within the functional paradigm, with well-typed abstractions and a solid understanding of the project’s business logic.
Branding: I begin the process of creating visual identity with an extensive interview, known as a briefing, which allows me to determine the real needs of my client, potential problems, and solutions that will emerge during the final design stage. I feel satisfaction from my work in this field only when both parties are pleased with the project—myself as the designer and the client. I have built my portfolio through a wide range of diverse projects, from comprehensive brand development (starting with naming, i.e., the process of creating a brand name), to visual identity design, corporate documents, logos, and even clothing labels.\n\nIt is important to me that the client understands how crucial it is to use not only the logo but the entire designed identity—the corporate identity—in a careful manner and in accordance with the brand book.
Graphic Design: In graphic design, I focus on combining a proper information architecture (highlighting the most important messages) with aesthetics that, beyond offering something visually appealing and hard to ignore, also contains humor, playfulness, and a sense of distance. I strive for my designs to subtly convey a deeper meaning, to be unmistakably original, and to be based on clean, legible typography. Less is more, and even less is more and more nowadays
Art: I don't claim to define myself as a musician, writer, or painter, but over the course of my work I have managed to complete several interesting projects with results that brought me a sense of satisfaction. Whether it was research and historical work on publishing a small book titled "Historie rodzinne," creating graffiti stencils in my hometown, or composing original music, in each of these cases I felt a strong need to realize these ideas, regardless of financial or time costs. Art for me is something that is priceless
